title: IBM, ORNL, and AMD Deploy Co-Located Quantum Error Correction Platform in Poughkeepsie - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IBM, ORNL's Quantum Science Center and AMD co-located a 120-qubit Nighthawk r2 QPU with ORNL's AMD-powered Umbra HPC system in Poughkeepsie to enable sub-millisecond real-time QEC decoding. The testbed targets DOE Quantum Genesis Mission goals (70 to 100 logical qubits by 2028) and feeds IBM's 2029 Starling fault-tolerant roadmap.

insights.claim: IBM, the Quantum Science Center at Oak Ridge National Laboratory and AMD launched a quantum error correction co-design platform in Poughkeepsie, New York, that co-locates IBM's 120-qubit Nighthawk r2 processor with ORNL's Umbra HPC system powered by AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs and 5th Gen AMD EPYC CPUs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: AMD gains a concrete foothold in quantum-classical hybrid infrastructure, an area where NVIDIA has been the default GPU partner.

insights.claim: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires classical decoders to process syndrome data fast enough to keep physical noise from overwhelming logical qubits, and sending syndrome telemetry over public cloud networks adds delays that rule out real-time conditional branching.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Implies fault-tolerant quantum systems will need dedicated co-located classical compute, shifting value toward on-prem HPC-plus-QPU deployments rather than pure cloud access.
insights.quote: transferring syndrome telemetry across public networks introduces transmission delays that preclude real-time conditional branching

insights.claim: Physical co-location of the Umbra cluster next to the dilution refrigerators enables sub-millisecond round-trip feedback loops so GPU-accelerated decoders can keep pace with the QPU's 100,000 circuits-per-second repetition rate.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Sets a concrete latency benchmark (sub-millisecond) that classical accelerators must meet to participate in QEC stacks.
insights.quote: Enables sub-millisecond round-trip feedback loops required for real-time syndrome processing
insights.locator: IBM / ORNL / AMD QEC Co-Design Platform

insights.claim: On the classical side, the platform uses the AMD ROCm open software ecosystem and AMD Versal adaptive SoCs to pipeline syndrome readout directly into GPU memory.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: AMD is using QEC decoding as a showcase for ROCm and FPGA-class Versal parts, a potential new demand vector for its adaptive-compute line.
insights.locator: The co-design testbed focuses on scaling

insights.claim: The platform is aligned with the DOE Quantum Genesis Mission (Q Competition), which targets scaling from 70 logical qubits running 438 operations to 100 logical qubits across 100,000 operations by 2028.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A US government program with explicit logical-qubit milestones by 2028 creates a funded demand pull and a public yardstick to measure vendors against.
insights.quote: Targets scaling from 70 logical qubits (438 operations) to 100 logical qubits across 100,000 operations by 2028
insights.locator: IBM / ORNL / AMD QEC Co-Design Platform

insights.claim: The testbed focuses on hierarchical error-correcting codes in which an inner topological code protects localized physical qubit clusters and an outer code mitigates correlated spatial errors across modules.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hierarchical codes point to a modular architecture, which is how IBM plans to scale toward Starling.
insights.locator: The co-design testbed focuses on scaling

insights.claim: The Poughkeepsie testbed is the integrated compute foundation informing IBM's roadmap toward IBM Quantum Starling, its modular fault-tolerant system planned for 2029.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Ties a near-term deployment to IBM's 2029 fault-tolerance target, a key milestone for IBM's quantum valuation narrative.
insights.locator: The testbed establishes the integrated compute

insights.claim: Early scientific targets of the IBM-ORNL-AMD platform are condensed matter physics and neutron scattering, matching quantum time-evolution simulations against data from ORNL's Spallation Neutron Source to model frustrated magnetic materials.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: National labs are pairing quantum simulation with existing experimental facilities, giving materials science the clearest early validation path.
insights.locator: The co-design testbed focuses on scaling

insights.claim: The Poughkeepsie testbed also connects to ORNL's Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility, linking IBM quantum hardware into US leadership-class supercomputing infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Integration with flagship DOE supercomputing centers strengthens IBM's position for government quantum procurement.
insights.locator: The testbed establishes the integrated compute
